question: When did Jesus ascend into heaven?
summary: Luke 24:51 has Jesus ascend on the day of resurrection itself, after a single day of post-resurrection appearances. Mark 16:19 has the ascension at the close of a sequence of appearances. John 20:26 has Jesus still on earth eight days after the resurrection, appearing to Thomas. Acts 13:31 has him appearing for many days before ascending. Acts 1:3 specifies forty days. The New Testament gives at least four different timelines for the ascension.

reconcile.connective: Clarke slots all eight post-resurrection appearances into one ordered sequence, placing Luke's ascension scene last, within the forty days.

discrepancy.connective: Mikeal Parsons argues Luke narrated the ascension twice with two different timelines because the rhetorical needs of the Gospel and Acts differed.

skeptic.name: Mikeal C. Parsons
skeptic.work: The Departure of Jesus in Luke-Acts: The Ascension Narratives in Context
skeptic.attribution: Mikeal C. Parsons, The Departure of Jesus in Luke-Acts: The Ascension Narratives in Context, JSNTSup 21 (Sheffield: JSOT Press, 1987)

pd_work.resource: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832)
pd_work.author: Adam Clarke
pd_work.note: Clarke's note on Acts 1:3 treats this exact tension directly, reproducing Bishop Pearce's numbered harmony of all post-resurrection appearances (Matthew, Mark, Luke, John, Acts, 1 Corinthians 15) to show Luke 24:50's ascension falls at the end of the forty-day period rather than on resurrection day.

excerpts.attribution: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832)
excerpts.excerpt_text: The several appearances of Jesus Christ, during the forty days of his sojourning with his disciples, between his resurrection and ascension, are thus enumerated by Bishop Pearce: The first was to Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, Mat 28:1-9. … The fifth was to the eleven disciples, Thomas being then with them, Joh 20:26. … The eighth, when they were assembled together, and when he led them unto Bethany, Luk 24:50, from whence he ascended to heaven.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly reconciles the multiple ascension timelines named in the contradiction by ordering all eight post-resurrection appearances into one sequence, placing Luke 24:50's ascension as the final (eighth) event within Acts 1:3's forty-day span and explicitly citing John 20:26 as an intervening appearance.
excerpts.source_note_text:
To whom - he showed himself alive - by many infallible proofs - Πολλοις τεκμηριοις; by many proofs of such a nature, and connected with such circumstances, as to render them indubitable; for this is the import of the Greek word τεκμηριον. The proofs were such as these:
1. Appearing to several different persons at different times.
2. His eating and drinking with them.
3. His meeting them in Galilee according to his own appointment.
4. His subjecting his body to be touched and handled by them.
5. His instructing them in the nature and doctrines of his kingdom.
6. His appearing to upwards of five hundred persons at once, Co1 15:6. And,
7. Continuing these public manifestations of himself for forty days.
The several appearances of Jesus Christ, during the forty days of his sojourning with his disciples, between his resurrection and ascension, are thus enumerated by Bishop Pearce:
The first was to Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, Mat 28:1-9.
The second, to the two disciples on their way to Emmaus, Luk 24:15.
The third, to Simon Peter, Luk 24:34.
The fourth, to ten of the apostles, Thomas being absent, Luk 24:36, and Joh 20:19. (All these four appearances took place on the day of his resurrection.)
The fifth was to the eleven disciples, Thomas being then with them, Joh 20:26.
The sixth, to seven of the apostles in Galilee, at the sea of Tiberias, Joh 21:4.
The seventh, to James, Co1 15:7, most probably in Jerusalem, and when Jesus gave an order for all his apostles to assemble together, as in Act 1:4.
The eighth, when they were assembled together, and when he led them unto Bethany, Luk 24:50, from whence he ascended to heaven. But see the note on Joh 21:14, for farther particulars.
Pertaining to the kingdom of God - Whatever concerned the doctrine, discipline, and establishment of the Christian Church.
